questions.question: A cistern has a leak which would empty it in 6 hours. A tap is turned on which admits 10 litres of water per minute into the cistern. When it is full it is now emptied in 10 hours. What is the capacity (in litres) of the cistern?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Time for inlet tap alone = (10 × 6) ÷ (10 − 6) = 60 ÷ 4 = 15 hours

Inlet rate = 10 litres/min = 600 litres/hour

Capacity of cistern = 15 hours × 600 litres/hour = 9000 litres

**∴ The correct answer is 9000 litres.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Time taken by leak to empty tank = 6 hours

Time taken by (leak + inlet) to empty tank = 10 hours

Filling rate of inlet tap = 10 litres/min

**Formula Used:**

Efficiency = Total Work ÷ Time

Capacity = Rate × Time

 
 

 **Person**
 **Days (hrs)**
 **Total Work**
 **Efficiency**
 
 

 Leak (A)
 6
 30
 −5
 
 

 Leak + Inlet (A+B)
 10
 −3
 
 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Efficiency of Leak A = −5 units/hr (negative because it empties)

⇒ Combined Efficiency of Leak A and Inlet B = −3 units/hr

⇒ Efficiency of Inlet B = Combined Efficiency − Efficiency of Leak A

⇒ Efficiency of Inlet B = −3 − (−5) = 2 units/hr (positive because it fills)

⇒ Time taken by Inlet B to fill the tank alone = 30 ÷ 2 = 15 hours

⇒ Total time in minutes = 15 × 60 = 900 minutes

⇒ Capacity of the cistern = Rate × Total time = 10 × 900 = 9000 litres

**∴ The correct answer is 9000 litres.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Pipes and Cisterns Efficiency

Inlet pipes have positive efficiency (+), while outlet pipes or leaks have negative efficiency (−). The net work is the sum of their efficiencies.

Capacity Formula

The capacity of a tank is determined by: Volume = Flow Rate × Time. Ensure all time units are consistent (e.g., minutes with litres/min).

Combined Work for Opposite Nature

If pipe A fills in x hours and pipe B empties in y hours, and y > x, the tank is filled in (xy) ÷ (y − x) hours.

questions.question: A man covers a certain distance at a speed of 60 km/h and returns at a speed of 40 km/h. What is his average speed (in km/h) for the entire journey?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] **__Shortcut Trick__**

Average speed = 2ab/(a + b)

Where a and b is speed

⇒ (2 times 60 times 40) over 60 + 40 = 48 km/h

**∴ Average speed is 48 km/h**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] __Alternate Method__**Given:

Certain distance at a speed = 60 km/h 

Returns of same distance at a speed = 40 km/h

**Formula used:**

Average speed = Total distance / Total time

**Calculation:**

Let distance = a km

⇒ Time = a/60 h

⇒ Time taken on return = a/40

⇒ Total distance = a + a = 2a

Total time taken = a/60 + a/40

⇒ (2a + 3a) / 120

⇒ 5a/120

⇒ a/24

Average speed = 2a times 24over a = 48 km/h

∴ Average speed is 48 km/h

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e085a7f17645c801966c030eb44d69fae944b96fdb4c4077f5fba1bc2c24bc71.png] **__Mistake Points__**If both direction cover same distance then use,

Average speed = 2ab/(a + b)

Where a and b is speed

Otherwise go with alternate solution.

questions.question: A shopkeeper bought 60 kg of rice at ₹42 per kg and mixed it with 120 kg rice at ₹52 per kg. At what rate (₹ per kg) should he sell the mixture to gain 20%?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] **__Shortcut Trick__**

CP of mixture = (60 x 42 + 120 x 52)/ 60 + 120

⇒ 8760/180 = Rs. 48.66 per kg

⇒ SP on 20% profit = 48.66 x 120/100 = 58.40 per kg

**∴ Required rate is 58.40 per kg.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] __Alternate Method__**Given:

A shopkeeper bought 60 kg of rice at ₹42 per kg 

and120 kg rice at ₹52 per kg

**Formula used:**

Selling price at profit = Cost price x (100 + profit%)/100

**Calculation:**

Price of 60 kg rice = 60 x 42 = Rs. 2520

Price of 120 kg rice = 120 x 52 = Rs. 6240

Now mix the the both rice then

⇒ Price of mixture per kg = (2520 + 6240) / (60 + 120)

⇒ 8760/180 = Rs. 48.66 per kg

Selling price of per kg on 20% profit = 48.66 x (100 + 20)/100

⇒ 48.66 x 120/100

⇒ Rs. 58.40 per kg

∴ Required rate is 58.40 per kg.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**Profit = Selling price - Cost price

Profit% = [(Selling price - Cost price) × 100] ÷ Cost price

Selling price at profit = Cost price x (100 + profit%)/100

Loss = Cost price - Selling price

Loss% = [(Cost price - Selling price) × 100] ÷ Cost price

Selling price at loss = Cost price x (100 - loss%)/100

Selling price at discount = Marked Price x (100 - discount%)/100

questions.question: If the difference between the simple interest and compound interest on a sum of money invested for 2 years at the rate of 15% per annum (interest compound annually) is ₹225, then what is the sum?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] **__Shortcut Trick__**

Difference between CI and SI for 2 years = Principle x r²/(100)²

⇒ 225 = P times 15 times 15 over 100 times 100

⇒ P = Rs. 10000

**∴ Sum is Rs. 10000.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__****Given:**

Difference between CI and SI for 2 years = Rs. 225

Rate of interest (R) = 15% per annum

Time = 2 years

**Formula used:**

Simple interest = (P x R x T)/100, and

Compound Interest = [P (1 + R/100)T- P]

Where P = Principle or Sum

R = Rate of interest per annum

T= Time

**Calculation:**

Let Sum = P

⇒ SI = P x 15 x 2/100 = 30P/100

⇒ CI = P (1 + 15/100)² - P

⇒ P (23/20)² - P

⇒ 529P - 400P/400

⇒ 129P/400

According to question,

Difference between CI and SI for 2 years:

⇒ 225 = ​​129P/400 - 30P/100​

⇒ 225 = (129P - 120P)/400

⇒ 225 = 9P/400

⇒ P = Rs. 10000

∴ Sum is Rs. 10000.

questions.question: Two ropes, one 8 m long and the other 14 m long are to be cut into pieces of the same length. What will the maximum possible length of each piece be?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Two rope length = 8 m and 14 m

**Calculation:**

⇒ 8 = 2 x 2 x 2

⇒ 14 = 2 x 7

⇒ HCF (Highest Common Factor) of 8 and 14 = 2

**∴ Maximum possible length of each piece is 2 m.**

questions.question: The capacities of two hemispherical vessel are 2.7 litres and 12.5 litres. Find the ratio of the areas of the inner curved surface of the vessels.
questions.solution:
Given:

Capacity means volume of one hemisphere = 2.7 ltr

Capacity means volume of another hemisphere = 12.5 ltr

**Formula used:**

Volume of hemisphere = 2πr3/3

Curved surface are of hemisphere = 2πr2

Total surface area = 3πr2

1 liter = 1000 cm3

**Calculation:**

 (2)/(3) x (22)/(7) x r₁³ = 2.7 ltr x 1000 cm³ = 2700 

⇒ r₁³ = (675 x 21/11)

⇒ r1 = (675 x 21/11)1/3

Now 

⇒ (2)/(3) x (22)/(7) x r₂3 = 12.5 ltr x 1000 cm3 = 12500

⇒ r₂³ = (3125 x 21/11)

⇒ r2 = (3125 x 21/11)1/3

Required ratio,

⇒ r₁ : r₂ = (675 x 21/11)¹/³ : (3125 x 21/11)¹/³ = 3 : 5

Ratio of the area of the inner curved surface = 2πr₁2/2πr₂2

⇒ r12/r22

⇒ (3/5)² = 9 ∶ 25

**∴ Required ratio is 9 : 25.**

questions.question: An electric heater was sold at a profit of 12%. If its cost had been 5% less and it had been sold for ₹180 less, the profit would have been 10%. What is the cost price of the electric heater?

⇒ first sp on 12% profit = 112

Now new cp at 5% less = 95

⇒ new sp = 95 x 110/100 = 104.5

Difference between first sp and new sp = Rs. 180

⇒ cp = 100 x 24 = Rs. 2400

According to question,

questions.question: The interest on a certain deposit at 3.5% per annum will be ₹210 in one year. How much will the additional interest in one year be on the same deposit at 4% per annum?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] **__Shortcut Trick__**

If 3.5 = 210

⇒ 1 = 60

⇒ 4 = 4 x 60 = 240

Additional interest = 240 - 210 = Rs.30

**∴ Additional interest in one year is Rs.30**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] __Alternate Method__**Given:

Initial R = 3.5%

Initial interest = Rs. 210

New R = 4%

**Formula used:**

Simple Interest = (Principle × Rate per annum ×Time)/100

**Calculation:**

Let deposit = Rs. a 

⇒ 210 = (a x 3.5 x 1)/100

⇒ a = 6000

Now,

Simple interest on 4% = (6000 x 4 x 1)/100

⇒ 240

Additional interest = 240 - 210 = Rs. 30

∴ Additional interest in one year is Rs. 30

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **__Important Points__** Simple interest = (Principle x Rate per annum x Time)/100

Amount = Simple interest + Principle

questions.question: The ratio of the monthly incomes of Ramu and Somu is 6 : 5 and the ratio of their expenditures is 7 : 6. At the end of the month, Ramu and Somu save ₹1,500 and ₹1,000, respectively. What is Ramu's monthly income?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Monthly income ratio of Ramu and Somu = 6 : 5

Ration of their expenditure = 7 : 6

Savings of Ramu and Somu = 1500 and 1000

**Concept used:**

Monthly income - expenditure = Savings 

**Calculation:**

Let Ramu's monthly income = 6a

⇒ Somu monthly income = 5a

According to question,

6a - 1500 over 5a - 1000 = 7 over 6

⇒ 36a - 9000 = 35a - 7000

⇒ a = 2000

Monthly income of Ramu = 6a

⇒ 6 x 2000 = Rs.12000 

**∴ Monthly income of Ramu is Rs.12000.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] **__Shortcut Trick__** 

6x - 1500 over 5x - 1000 = 7 over 6

⇒ 36x - 9000 = 35x - 7000

⇒ x = 2000

Monthly income of Ramu = 6 x 2000 =Rs.12000 

∴ Monthly income of Ramu is Rs.12000.

questions.question: Mukul lent ₹9,300 on simple interest in two parts. He earned 5% per annum on the first part and 8% per annum on the second part. The total interest he received after 4 years is ₹2,400. What is the ratio of the money lent at 5% to that lent at 8%?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] **__Shortcut Trick__**

Let total amount give on 5%, then SI for 1 year = 9300 x 5 x 1 /100 = 465

Again Let total amount give on 8%, then SI for 1 year = 9300 x 8 x 1/100 = 744

Total interest in 4 year = 2400

Interest for 1 year = 2400/4 = 600

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/49c57946dbf842b1430c1646fa1a90ff04bcfe2dd555d9401b7ff99ccdd2c8e4.png] 

Required Ratio = 144 : 135 = 16 : 15

**∴ Required Ratio = 16 : 15.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] __Alternate Method__**Given:

Total principle = Rs. 9300

Interest at 4 years = Rs. 2400

**Formula used:**

Simple interest = (Principle x Rate per annum x Time)/100

**Calculation:**

Let money lent on 5% = a

⇒ Then money lent on 8% = 9300 - a

Interest on 4 year = 2400

⇒ then interest on 1 year = 2400/4

⇒ Rs. 600

According to question,

(a times 5 times 1)/(100) + ((9300 - a) times 8 times 1)/(100) = 600

⇒ (5a)/(100) + (74400 - 8a)/(100) = 600

⇒ (-3a + 74400)/(100) = 600

⇒ - 3a + 74400 = 60000

⇒ 3a = 14400

⇒ a = 4800

Now money lent on 5% = a = 4800

⇒ Money lent on 8% = 9300 - 4800 = 4500

Required ratio = 4800 : 4500

∴ Required Ratio = 16 : 15.

questions.question: If the difference between two numbers is 42 and their LCM and HCF are 1729 and 7, respectively, what is the sum of those two numbers?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] **__Shortcut Trick__**Let the number be 7a and 7b, where a and b are co-prime numbers

⇒ 7 x 1729 = 7a x 7b

⇒ ab = 247 = 13 x 19

Then possible numbers are

⇒ 7a = (7 x 13) or (7 x 247)

⇒ 7b = (7 x 19) or (7 x 1)

⇒ Sum of these two numbers = 91 + 133 = 224

∴ Sum of these two numbers is 224

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

HCF = 7

LCM = 1729

Difference between two numbers = 42

**Formula used:**

HCF x LCF = Product of numbers

**Calculation:**

Let the number be 7a and 7b, where a and b are co-prime numbers

Now, 

HCF x LCF = Product of numbers

⇒ 7 x 1729 = 7a x 7b

⇒ ab = 247

a and b are co-prime, so 

a could be either 13 or 247

b could be either 19 or 1

Then possible numbers are

⇒ 7a = (7 x 13) or (7 x 247)

⇒ 7b = (7 x 19) or (7 x 1)

According to option

We take 7a = 7 x 13 = 91

⇒ 7b = 7 x 19 = 133

⇒ Sum of these two numbers = 91 + 133 = 224

**∴ Sum of these two numbers is 224.**

questions.question: The price of sugar rises by 33%. By what percent should a family reduce the consumption of sugar, so as NOT to increase the expenditure?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

 Trick = (Increase% x 100) ÷ (100 + Increase%)

⇒ (33 x 100) ÷ (100 + 33)

⇒ (33 × 100)/(133) = 24.8%

**∴ Required % is 24.8%.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] __Alternate Method - 1__**Given:

Price of sugar rises = 33%.

Concept used:

​Selling price at profit = Cost price x (100 + profit%)/100

**Calculation:**

Let initial price of sugar = 100

⇒ Initial consumption = 100

⇒ Total expenditure = price x consumption

⇒ 100 x 100 = 10000

Now new price of sugar after increase of 33% = 100 + 33 = 133

But new expenditure is remain same = 10000

⇒ New consumption = expenditure ÷ new price

⇒ New consumption = 10000/133

⇒ % Decrease in consumption = 100 - 10000/133 = 3300/133

**∴ % Decrease in consumption is 24.8.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] __Alternate Method - 2__**** ****Given:**

Price of sugar rises = 33%.

**Concept used:**

Selling price at profit = Cost price x (100 + profit%)/100

Calculation:

Let initial price of sugar = Rs, A

⇒ Initial consumption = B

⇒ Total expenditure = price x consumption

⇒ Total expenditure = A x B = AB

Now new price of sugar after increase of 33% = A x (100 + 33) /100

⇒ 133A/100

⇒ New expenditure is remain same = AB

⇒ New consumption = expenditure ÷ new price

⇒ New consumption = (AB × 100)/(133A) = 100B/133

⇒ Decrease in consumption = B - 100B/133

⇒ 33B/133

⇒ % Decrease in consumption = (33B times 100)/(133 times B) = 24.8

∴ % Decrease in consumption is 24.8.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **__Important Points__**Profit = Selling price - Cost price

Profit% = [(Selling price - Cost price) × 100] ÷ Cost price

Selling price at profit = Cost price x (100 + profit%)/100

Loss = Cost price - Selling price

Loss% = [(Cost price - Selling price) × 100] ÷ Cost price

Selling price at loss = Cost price x (100 - loss%)/100

questions.question: What will be single discount equivalent to three successive discounts of 50%, 30% and 20%?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] **__Shortcut Trick__**

If successive discount a% and b%

equivalent discount = a + b - ab/100

⇒ 50 + 30 - 50 x 30/100 = 65%

⇒ 65 + 20 - 65 x 20/100 = 72%

∴ Equivalent discount is 72%

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__****Given:**

Successive discount = 50%, 30% and 20%

**Concept used:**

If successive discount a% and b%

equivalent discount = a + b - ab/100

**Calculation:**

Let total value = 100

First discount 50% = 100 x 50/100 = 50

⇒ Remaining = 100 - 50 = 50

Second discount 30% on remaining 50 = 50 x 30/100 = 15

⇒ Remaining = 50 - 15 = 35 

Third discount 20% on remaining 35 = 35 x 20/100 = 7

⇒ Total discount = 50 + 15 + 7 = 72%

**∴ Equivalent discount is 72%**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__**Successive discount means discount on the discount. (just like Compound Interest rate= interest on interest)

If the first discount is a% and 2nd discount is b% then,

Total discount = (a + b - ab/100) %

questions.question: A can complete 2 over 3 of a work in 10 days and B can complete 4 over 5 of the same work in 8 days. They work together for 5 days. The remaining work is completed by C alone in 6 days. In how many days C alone can complete 75% of the same work?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] **__Shortcut Trick__**

For A,

2/3 = 10 ⇒ 1 = 15 days 

A can complete total work = 15 days

For B,

4/5 = 8 ⇒ 1 = 10 days

B can complete total work = 10 days

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/1808754ac89d78eb73f44b8747b2ef08131488e28b80c0d2a0bcebb157d6810b.png] 

(A + B) can do work together 5 days = 5 (2 + 3) = 25 

Remaining work = 30 - 25 = 5 

Now For C, 6 days = 5

Efficiency of C ⇒ 1 days = 5/6

C can done 75% of total work = (30 times 75)/(100) div (5)/(6) = (45)/(2) times (6)/(5) = 27

**∴ C can done 75% of total work in 27 days.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] __Alternate Method__**Given:

A can complete 2 over 3 of a work = 10 days

B can complete 4 over 5 of the same work in 8 days

They work together for 5 days

**Concept used:**

Efficiency of men = Total work / Total days

**Calculation:**

For A can complete 2/3 work = 10

⇒ A can complete total work = 15 days

⇒ A can done work in 1 day = 1/15

For B can complete 4/5 work = 8

⇒ B can complete total work = 10 days

⇒ B can done work in 1 day = 1/10

⇒ (A + B) work done in 5 days = 5 x (1/15 + 1/10) 

⇒ 25/30

Here total work is LCM of 15 and 10 = 30

⇒ (A + B) work done in 5 days = 25

⇒ Remaining work = 30 - 25 = 5

Now C can do remaining work 5 = 6 days 

⇒ Efficiency of C = 5/6

⇒ C can done 75% of total work = (30 times 75)/(100) div (5)/(6) = (45)/(2) times (6)/(5) = 27

∴ C can done 75% of total work in 27 days.

questions.question: The mean of 15 measurements was calculated to be 50 cm. But it was found that one of the measurements was recorded as 46 cm instead of 61 cm. What is the correct mean (in cm)?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] **__Shortcut Trick__**

Difference of wrong measurements = 61 - 46 = 15 cm

⇒ Mean variation = 15 ÷ 15 = 1 cm

⇒ New mean = 50 + 1 = 51 cm

**∴ Correct mean is 51 cm.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] __Alternate Method__**Given:

Total measurements = 15

Initial mean = 50 cm

**Formula used:**

Average / Mean = Sum of observation / Number of observation

Sum of observation = Average x number of observation 

Mean variation = Difference ÷ Total measurements

**Calculation:**

Sum of observation 15 x 50 =750 cm

Difference of wrong measurements = 61 - 46 = 15 cm

New sum of observation = 750 + 15 = 765

Correct mean = 765/15

⇒ 51 cm

∴ Correct mean is 51 cm.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e085a7f17645c801966c030eb44d69fae944b96fdb4c4077f5fba1bc2c24bc71.png] **__Mistake Points__**

If mistaken observation is less than real observation than mean variation = (real observation - mistaken observation)/ Total number of observation and in this condition correct mean is always higher than incorrect mean.

If mistaken observation is more than real observation than mean variation = (mistaken observation - real observation)/ Total number of observation and in this condition correct mean is always less than incorrect mean.

questions.question: A car starts at a speed of 80 km/h, with its speed increasing by 8 km/h every two hours. In how many hours will it cover 432 km?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] **__Shortcut Trick__ **

 
 

 
 ** Speed**
 ** Distance**
 
 

 Speed for first 2 hours
 80 km/h
 80 x 2 = 160 km
 
 

 Speed for next 2 hours
 80 + 8 = 88 km/h
 88 x 2 = 176 km
 
 

 Speed for next 1 hour
 88 + 8 = 96 km/h
 96 x 1 = 96 km
 
 

 **Total hours = 5** 
 
 **Total distance = 432 km**
 
 

** ∴ Total hours for cover 432 km is 5 hours. **

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] __Alternate Method__**Speed for first 2 hours = 80 km/h

⇒ Distance cover in first 2 hours = 80 x 2 = 160 km

Speed for next 2 hours = 80 + 8 = 88 km/h

⇒ Distance cover in first 2 hours = 88 x 2 = 176

⇒ Distance cover in total 4 hour = 160 + 176 = 336 km

⇒ Remaining distance = 432 - 336 = 96 km

Then we know speed for next hour = 88 + 8 = 96 km/h

If we drive only one hour then we cover last 96 km.

⇒ Total hour for cover 432 km = 2 + 2 + 1 = 5 hours

 ∴ Total hours for cover 432 km is 5 hours.
